summary: Revision correctly restores the integrated programme, separates owners, removes the figure-gate circularity and keeps null/negative honesty. Remaining design-level blockers: no research-apparatus tier (F1) and a primary outcome that may not observe G's mechanism at all given harness-noise evidence in the bundle (F2). Majors: run-class boundary (F3), UNKNOWN differential missingness (F4), hidden sealing/contamination (F5), block/variance plan (F6), operational arm deltas (F7), first-class feasibility outcome (F8). A staged smaller study (single-arm feasibility -> B/C/G dev -> C vs G confirmation) is recommended.

findings.title: Research apparatus tier undefined (where B/C/G, evidence store, run adapter, scorer physically run)
findings.problem: Study requires runnable apparatus; native construction is paused; Python oracles are not runtime; no tier/authority for the experimental apparatus is declared. Produces an endless readiness loop.
findings.alternative_explanation: Root may intend existing Prime Agent prompts/skills/REPL services as the apparatus without native change; this is simply unstated.
findings.change: Add an explicit research-apparatus tier: project-local, disposable, non-native (prompt packs + Python skill modules + REPL/file journal services); not counted as ARGO native construction; code hash enters protocol fingerprint; mark each owner-port as apparatus-realized vs native-design-only.
findings.closure_evidence: Apparatus tier decision record with permitted scope/prohibitions; hash-bound runnable B/C/G manifests.

findings.title: Primary outcome vs G-specific mechanism signal-to-noise mismatch
evidence: paper/research/long-horizon-harness-benchmark-20260907/sources/2608.23552v1-layout.txt:L456-457 (harness choice had little effect on final records vs noise, 2-3 seeds; author-reported)
paper/sources/tex/2606.11926/main.tex:L823-832 (Arbor tree/insight ablation on 11 MLE-Bench Lite tasks; author-reported, not a power prior)
findings.problem: G's increment (scoped invalidation, graph-mediated continuation) fires mainly on revision/restart events, but primary is natural campaign with stress as secondary strata. Risk of null-by-construction or noise-dominated primary; moving stress into primary post hoc would favour G by construction.
findings.alternative_explanation: G may improve candidate selection/pruning without revision events (Arbor-like); then natural primary is correct. Must be checked in development before fixing confirmation primary.
findings.change: Include an arm-common preregistered event schedule inside the task definition (e.g., dataset version bump, baseline defect disclosure, one fresh-context restart at fixed decision indices). Primary = hidden performance of final artifact over the event-inclusive campaign; natural-only stratum labeled secondary. Estimate within-cell variance and MUE-vs-noise in development.
findings.closure_evidence: Task certificate with event schedule hash; blinded dev variance/MUE table; preregistered statement that G-C expected effect is ~0 absent dependency events.

findings.title: Scientific-run class boundary undefined between ORX authority runs and local REPL analyses
findings.problem: Local analyses that change decisions become unreceipted scientific runs; routing all computation through ORX makes turnaround dominate the dependency horizon and multiplies UNKNOWN exposure.
findings.alternative_explanation: Root may intend only artifact-producing train/eval as scientific runs; then a recording rule for local analyses is still missing.
findings.change: Two-class rule: R1 authority runs (artifact-producing train/eval) require ORX receipts; R2 local analyses are journaled with code/input/output hashes. Every number cited by a decision node must reference an R1 or R2 receipt. 'No second run registry' applies to R1 only.
findings.closure_evidence: Run-class rule in protocol; failing-first audit fixture rejecting decision nodes citing unreceipted numbers.

findings.title: Infrastructure UNKNOWN creates treatment-correlated missingness
findings.problem: UNKNOWN is neither failure nor not-run and is never retried, so the arm loses an opportunity through infrastructure; exposure scales with launch count and thus with arm. invalid_handling is null.
findings.alternative_explanation: UNKNOWN may be rare; but the only existing ORX record is a stale running record, so rarity cannot be assumed.
findings.change: Treatment-blind three-class rule: unresolved infra-UNKNOWN/BLOCKED voids the whole programme block (all arms) as INFRA_VOID, reported in census; protocol-invalid gets floor score under ITT; scientific failure keeps real score. Human resolution allowed, arm-blind, logged as intervention.
findings.closure_evidence: Filled invalid_handling; receipt of blind application on development logs; ITT/per-protocol sensitivity plan.

findings.title: Hidden means access-hidden not knowledge-hidden; no sealing procedure for a single-operator project
findings.problem: Public test splits may be in pretraining (shrinks room for evidence-control effects); same human tunes apparatus on dev and prepares hidden split; no commitment.
findings.alternative_explanation: A private re-split or post-cutoff data partially restores knowledge hiding.
findings.change: Task certificate: prefer private re-split/post-cutoff; contamination statement plus pre-run canary if public test used; hash commitment of hidden split and scorer code before development; hidden-open log.
findings.closure_evidence: Commitment receipt; contamination statement; zero-change audit after hidden open.

findings.title: No block/paired design or variance-component plan
findings.problem: Programme-as-unit is right, but within-programme blocking of all arms (same baseline/seeds) and separate estimation of between-programme vs within-cell variance are absent. Nested variance estimation logically needs >=2 independent starts in some cells; this is a design requirement, not a sample floor.
findings.alternative_explanation: Root may already intend family-level paired analysis (MS-B3 closure text) without writing it into the design.
findings.change: Specify programme=block, all arms per block, randomized order, paired block differences with cluster/randomization interval; development estimates variance components; confirmation precision plan derived only from those estimates; no numeric floors.
findings.closure_evidence: Blinded precision worksheet with variance components; block/randomization receipt.

findings.title: Operational B/C/G deltas absent; compulsory vs graph-control not yet separable
findings.problem: Unclear whether 'compulsory' is prompt instruction or tool gating, and whether G's continuation is a deterministic affected-set tool or LLM reading a graph. C-B may become prompt-vs-harness and G-C a mix of representation, deterministic computation and context shape.
findings.alternative_explanation: Any G advantage may come from deterministic dependency computation, compressed active view, or extra check opportunities rather than graph representation (agrees with all five reviews).
findings.change: Arm-difference table (representation / enforced gates / tools incl. whether C gets equivalent tools over the tree / prompt bytes / capsule generator / context byte ceiling); implement C's compulsory checks as tool gating; log every G graph-capability invocation for mechanism attribution; passive-graph arm only if logs cannot disambiguate.
findings.closure_evidence: Hash-bound arm-difference table; code-path activation receipts; delivered-vs-used evidence instrumentation.

findings.title: Integrated-system contribution lacks a first-class feasibility outcome
findings.problem: Only control policy is a causal treatment; all system layers are fixed. Without a reportable end-to-end feasibility result the integrated-system claim is descriptive and reads as memory ablation plus system description.
findings.alternative_explanation: Owner-contract design could be framed as a contribution by itself, but without evidence it is indistinguishable from the feature stack the user rejected.
findings.change: Define Stage 0 single-arm feasibility as a reportable outcome: completion of a real public ML campaign through the full loop with ORX receipt and sealed scoring, completion rate, failure anatomy, full cost. Frame paper contribution as (i) loop feasibility/failure anatomy, (ii) causal C-vs-G contrast, (iii) owner-contract design.
findings.closure_evidence: Stage 0 protocol with completion definition and census schema; result receipt.

findings.title: Prototype default under inconclusive outcome and cross-instance coupling to native resume gate not recorded
findings.problem: Inconclusive maps to 'no winner' only; PrototypeReadiness depends on native construction resume gates that are tied to an unrelated test instance (DeepVoice) per harness policy, so a NAIS prototype could be blocked regardless of this study.
findings.alternative_explanation: Not circular; a deliberate but unstated dependency.
findings.change: Add mapping row: inconclusive -> prototype adopts cheapest arm passing Stage 0 feasibility, graph kept as audit/export, no efficacy claim. State the resume-gate dependency explicitly and raise decoupling as a user decision.
findings.closure_evidence: Decision-table row; explicit gate dependency statement.

findings.title: RD4 single execution approval does not match two-phase dev/confirmation
findings.problem: Development runs precede the frozen confirmation contract yet RD4 bundles both into one approval.
findings.alternative_explanation: Root may plan two approvals implicitly.
findings.change: Split RD4a (apparatus, dev families, dev budget) and RD4b (post-freeze confirmation).

findings.title: Two-part RQ with one primary; evidence-inheritance outcomes must be declared secondary
findings.problem: RQ names terminal performance and evidence inheritance; primary covers only the former.
findings.change: One sentence: continuation/inheritance diagnostics are secondary and are not promoted if primary is null.

findings.title: Human-adaptation leakage is counted but not prevented
findings.problem: Developer who tunes the apparatus on development families can steer it toward known confirmation families.
findings.alternative_explanation: Family ancestry split partially mitigates but does not hide identities.
findings.change: Seal the confirmation family list by hash commitment before development; reveal after freeze.

findings.title: Role of external runnable comparator (Arbor) must be fixed
findings.problem: In-house B risks 'weak baseline' critique; Arbor as an arm confounds substrate.
findings.alternative_explanation: Either choice is defensible depending on whether causal matching or external credibility is prioritized.
findings.change: Causal contrast uses in-house B/C/G on the same substrate; optional Arbor matched-run reported only as a labeled non-causal external anchor if budget permits; no SOTA ranking.
findings.closure_evidence: Comparator role statement in protocol; if used, Arbor run manifest with substrate differences declared.

findings.title: 4/2/1 stress template status is handled correctly
findings.problem: None; noted so the numbers do not become de facto floors.
findings.change: Replace by task-specific event schedule per F2.

focus_answers.1_bcg_distinction_and_cost: Conceptually distinguishes compulsory process (C-B) from graph-control package (G-C); operationally undefined (F7). Three dev arms justified if they double as variance estimation; confirmation should default to C vs G.
focus_answers.2_integrated_vs_narrow: Causal content is a control-representation ablation; needs Stage 0 feasibility as a first-class result (F8). Topology-only claims are already correctly forbidden.
focus_answers.3_campaign_fit_gold_leakage: Eligibility criteria are sound; missing knowledge-hiding statement (F5), confirmation family sealing (F12), event schedule (F2). Arbor's MLE-Bench Lite ablation narrows novelty residual; be ready to frame as matched-rights reproduction-class evaluation.
focus_answers.4_selection_cost_nesting_power: Single preselected artifact and full cost are right; missing block design and variance components (F6), three-class invalid rule (F4). No numeric floors adopted (agree).
focus_answers.5_orx_authority_unknown: at-most-once vs exactly-once distinction is correct; missing run-class boundary (F3) and treatment-blind UNKNOWN rule (F4); stale running record shows the problem is live.
focus_answers.6_scorer_vs_critic: Separation correct; add human-operator sealing and artifact-environment manifest (F5).
focus_answers.7_gates: No remaining circularity; cross-instance coupling (F9) and approval split (F10).
focus_answers.8_feasible_path: Blocked mainly by F1; staged smaller study is the path.

decisions.reason: Programme selection without declaring graph the winner matches user invariants.

B/C/G screen and conditional passive arm accepted; requires operational arm-difference table (F7). SR-04 proposal to fix primary contrast as G-B is REJECTED in favour of root's freeze-after-development; add that C-vs-G is the default decisive contrast when budget limits arms.

Rejecting 6/24 floors is right; MS-B3 structural elements (paired, nested starts in development, ITT) are right and should be written into the design (F6). '>=2 starts in some cells' is a logical requirement of nested variance estimation, not a floor.
Natural-fit assessment alone risks a primary in which G's mechanism never fires (F2, supported by PA-NULL in the bundle). Recommend arm-common preregistered event schedule as part of task definition.
Add human-operator sealing/commitment and contamination statement (F5).
Add treatment-blind differential-missingness rule (F4); existing stale running record shows the issue is real.
Add run-class boundary between ORX authority runs and local analyses (F3).
Circular figure gate removal accepted; split RD4 approvals (F10).
Residual UNESTABLISHED is honest; SR-02 reclassification to reproduction/negative evaluation if residual absent is accepted; Arbor/EviGraph proximity makes that likely.
Runnable identity for in-house arms is mandatory; full reproduction of external comparators is optional and non-causal (F13).
Capability-invocation logging (F7) is the cheaper substitute; 2x2 only if logs cannot disambiguate.

not_addressed_by_sol_or_root: F2 primary-outcome SNR mismatch (PA-NULL evidence is in their own bundle)
F9 inconclusive prototype default and resume-gate coupling
preserved_disagreements: SR-04 (fix G-B as primary now) vs root (freeze after development): both defensible; this review sides with root but records the risk that a small development screen selects the wrong comparator.
MS-01 (2x2 pilot) vs root (conditional passive arm): if capability logs cannot attribute mechanism, MS-01 becomes correct.

smaller_decisive_study.stage_0: Single-arm feasibility (C recommended) on one public small-compute ML programme: complete the full loop (>=1 ORX R1 receipt, 1 sealed score, 1 refine->successor, 1 fresh-context restart); >=2 independent starts for first within-cell variance estimate; outputs completion, failure anatomy, full cost, variance. Failure to complete is itself a result and triggers a paper-scope decision, not indefinite repair.
smaller_decisive_study.stage_1: Development screen B/C/G with programme count derived from Stage 0 cost/variance (no numeric floor): verify arm manipulation, capability logs, event-schedule response, MUE vs noise, choose comparator.
smaller_decisive_study.stage_2: Confirmation on sealed programmes: C vs G (B only if development justifies), blocked design, single primary contrast, event-inclusive campaign final-artifact hidden performance.

adoption_rejection_rule.estimand: Mean programme-block paired difference (G-C) of final-artifact hidden performance over event-inclusive campaign, ITT with three-class invalid rule, cluster/randomization interval.
adoption_rejection_rule.adopt_G: interval lower bound > 0 AND point estimate >= MUE AND G/C full-cost ratio <= preregistered cap AND zero safety violations (hidden access, tampering).
adoption_rejection_rule.reject_G_choose_C: interval upper bound < MUE (gain excluded with adequate precision).
adoption_rejection_rule.inconclusive: interval covers both 0 and MUE -> prototype default = cheapest arm passing Stage 0; graph retained as audit/export; no efficacy claim.
adoption_rejection_rule.choose_B: only if non-inferior to C within preregistered margin and cheaper.
adoption_rejection_rule.post_hoc: any change to metric/selection/invalid rule after outcomes marks that analysis exploratory.

bounded_completion_rule: A. Stage 0 fails or the single preregistered repair budget is exhausted -> close as feasibility/failure-anatomy result; request paper-scope decision; no success relabeling.

B. Stage 0 completes, Stages 1-2 complete, every assigned block accounted as score/floor/INFRA_VOID, primary analysis and independent recomputation done, adoption rule applied -> close regardless of direction.
C. Total time/cost ceiling fixed at RD4a exhausted -> close at reached stage with the corresponding claim class.
Infrastructure readiness is never a completion criterion.

scope_limits: Opinion on design, methodology, feasibility, causal identification, lineage and claim boundaries; not efficacy, statistics, runtime certification or authority.
No execution, installation, subagent, network retrieval or new papers.
Working tree had uncommitted changes (docs/argo/agent-brief.md, paper/manuscript/thesis-ko.qmd, .planning/*); none were used. All inputs read from the immutable commit.
Author-reported numbers (Prime Agent PA-NULL, Arbor ablation) are cited as context for design risk only, not as local efficacy or power priors.
Reviewer agreement is not treated as scientific evidence; ratings are descriptive.
Only review.md and review.json were written.
